subject: jungle soldier
title: What If Nobody Told a Soldier the War Was Over? One Fought On Until 1974

scenes.text: What if a soldier never heard his war had ended? One kept fighting for 29 years.
December 1944. A Japanese intelligence officer lands on Lubang Island in the Philippines. His orders: never surrender.
The war ends eight months later. Leaflets fall from planes saying so. He decides they're an enemy trick.
Years pass. His three companions leave or die. Family letters arrive. He doesn't believe those either.
In 1974 a young Japanese traveler finds him. He says he'll stop only if his commander orders it.
His old major, now a bookseller, flies in and relieves him. He surrenders his sword, a working rifle, and 500 rounds.

description:
What if a soldier never accepted that his war was over? Hiroo Onoda, a Japanese intelligence officer, was sent to Lubang Island in the Philippines in December 1944 with orders never to surrender, and held out in the jungle until March 1974, nearly 29 years.
He dismissed leaflets and even family letters as enemy tricks. His group's raids are blamed for the deaths of up to 30 islanders. He stopped only when his former commander, by then a bookseller, came in person to relieve him; the Philippine president pardoned him.
